name: How do you choose between a shower pan and a fully tiled shower floor?

mainEntity.name: Should the new shower use a prefabricated pan or a custom tiled floor after a tub removal?
mainEntity.text: Should the new shower use a prefabricated pan or a custom tiled floor after a tub removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: A prefabricated shower pan is often the practical choice when the priorities are speed, lower maintenance, and predictable waterproofing. It can be a good fit for many tub-to-shower conversions because it simplifies the floor assembly. A fully tiled shower floor gives more design flexibility and a custom appearance, but it takes more labor and depends heavily on proper slope and waterproofing. Grout and tile also require more upkeep over time. Homeowners should weigh not only appearance but also long-term performance and cleaning. In a high-end bathroom, a tiled floor can help the shower feel more luxurious. In a secondary bath or accessibility-focused project, a pan may be the smarter option. The best answer depends on the room’s use, the budget, and the contractor’s proven installation method. Ask how each option affects timeline, cost, and warranty so the choice is made with full information.
acceptedAnswer.description: A shower pan is usually faster, simpler, and easier to maintain, while a tiled floor offers more design flexibility but needs more labor and careful waterproofing. The right choice depends on budget, style, and how much maintenance the homeowner wants.
